taxonomy.label: Cybersecurity and secure infrastructure
taxonomy.definition: Products that protect information systems, identities or networks, with documented use by defence, security or critical-infrastructure customers or programs.

taxonomy.label: Identity and access
taxonomy.definition: Authentication, credential, privileged-access and zero-trust products.

taxonomy.label: Threat detection and response
taxonomy.definition: Monitoring, detection, threat intelligence and incident-response software or services.

taxonomy.label: Cryptography and quantum-safe security
taxonomy.definition: Encryption products, key management and post-quantum or quantum-key-distribution security.

taxonomy.label: Secure systems and platforms
taxonomy.definition: Hardened operating systems, secure devices and cross-domain or classified-network products.

taxonomy.label: Communications and networking
taxonomy.definition: Communications hardware or software whose documented customers or programs include defence, public-safety or government users.

taxonomy.label: Secure networking
taxonomy.definition: Encrypted, resilient or tactical network equipment and software.

taxonomy.label: Radio and spectrum
taxonomy.definition: Radio systems, spectrum management, antennas and RF communications (not electronic attack).

taxonomy.label: Positioning, navigation and timing
taxonomy.definition: Resilient positioning, inertial navigation and timing for GNSS-degraded conditions.

taxonomy.label: Space, satellites and earth observation
taxonomy.definition: Space systems and space-derived data. Earth observation qualifies only with documented security, defence or sovereignty use; environmental monitoring alone does not (P-12).

taxonomy.label: Satellite communications
taxonomy.definition: Satellite communication networks, terminals and data relay.

taxonomy.label: Earth observation and geospatial intelligence
taxonomy.definition: Imaging, SAR and geospatial analytics with documented security or sovereignty use.

taxonomy.label: Space hardware and robotics
taxonomy.definition: Satellite buses, payloads, space robotics and components.

taxonomy.label: Launch and propulsion
taxonomy.definition: Launch vehicles, spaceports and space propulsion (not missile systems; P-15).

taxonomy.label: Space domain awareness
taxonomy.definition: Tracking and characterization of objects in orbit.

taxonomy.label: Logistics and supply-chain technology
taxonomy.definition: Technology for moving, sustaining or tracking materiel and assets, with documented defence or public-sector logistics use.

taxonomy.label: Supply-chain visibility
taxonomy.definition: Tracking, provenance and supply-chain risk software.

taxonomy.label: Fleet maintenance and sustainment
taxonomy.definition: Maintenance, condition monitoring and sustainment of vehicles, vessels and aircraft.

taxonomy.label: Sensors and sensing
taxonomy.definition: Sensing hardware and analytics with documented defence, security or public-safety use. General environmental monitoring alone does not qualify (P-12).

taxonomy.label: Maritime and underwater sensing
taxonomy.definition: Sonar, acoustic arrays, underwater vehicles' sensors and maritime domain awareness.

taxonomy.label: Optical, infrared and RF sensing
taxonomy.definition: Imagers, photonics, radar and RF sensing (not targeting or fire control; P-15).

taxonomy.label: Quantum sensing
taxonomy.definition: Quantum magnetometers, gravimeters and other quantum-enabled sensors.

taxonomy.label: Robotics and industrial automation (non-weaponized)
taxonomy.definition: Uncrewed systems and automation that are not weapons and carry no weapons payload. Counter-UAS interceptors and armed platforms are excluded (P-01).

taxonomy.label: Uncrewed aerial systems
taxonomy.definition: Non-weaponized drones for ISR, inspection, logistics or safety, and their autonomy software.

taxonomy.label: Ground and maritime robotics
taxonomy.definition: Uncrewed ground, surface and underwater vehicles that are not weapons.

taxonomy.label: Autonomy and perception software
taxonomy.definition: Navigation, perception and edge-AI software for robots.

taxonomy.label: Advanced materials and manufacturing
taxonomy.definition: Materials and production technology supplied to documented defence, aerospace or security programs. Energetics and munitions materials are excluded (P-15).

taxonomy.label: Advanced materials and coatings
taxonomy.definition: Composites, protective materials, signature-management coatings and nanomaterials.

taxonomy.label: Additive and precision manufacturing
taxonomy.definition: Additive manufacturing and precision production for aerospace and defence.

taxonomy.label: Electronics and semiconductors
taxonomy.definition: Ruggedized electronics, semiconductors and photonic chips.

taxonomy.label: Critical-infrastructure resilience
taxonomy.definition: Protection and continuity of energy, industrial and public infrastructure against attack or failure.

taxonomy.label: Energy and power resilience
taxonomy.definition: Deployable, off-grid or resilient power for critical or remote operations.

taxonomy.label: Industrial control security
taxonomy.definition: Security of operational technology and industrial control systems.

taxonomy.label: Emergency response and disaster support
taxonomy.definition: Tools for emergency services, search and rescue, CBRN protection and disaster response.

taxonomy.label: Incident coordination
taxonomy.definition: Command, coordination and situational-awareness software for responders.

taxonomy.label: Protective equipment and CBRN
taxonomy.definition: Protective equipment and CBRN detection and protection (not weapons).

taxonomy.label: Search and rescue technology
taxonomy.definition: Search-and-rescue equipment, sensing and platforms.

taxonomy.label: Other verifiable non-weapon dual-use
taxonomy.definition: Dual-use technology outside the segments above. Each case needs an especially explicit, documented rationale.

taxonomy.label: Simulation and training
taxonomy.definition: Simulation, synthetic environments and training systems (non-weapon).

taxonomy.label: Quantum computing
taxonomy.definition: Quantum computing hardware and software with documented security or defence relevance.

description.value: Ottawa software company whose ANVIL platform structures and stores intelligence data, enriches it with AI and delivers it to military users through mission applications; formerly IMRSV Data Labs.

eligibility.rationale: Ottawa developer of the ANVIL platform, AI-enabled software that links intelligence, operations and planning for national defence users; the company calls itself Canada's sovereign intelligence capability. Government data: a National Defence contract with Anvil Intelligence Inc. (CA$2,946,192.50, 17 July 2025, professional services, procurement W3330-26-2367), matched by exact name and postal area K1N to the grant rows that carry business number 817615776; and two National Research Council IRAP contributions (CA$0.9M and CA$2.0M, from December 2025 and February 2026). The Logic separately reports one disclosed National Defence contract of just under CA$3M. Software, not a weapons maker.

Montréal developer of superconducting quantum computing systems; its site lists Government and Defence among its markets and describes supporting national security and defence readiness. Documented defence-program link: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from CED (CA$600,000, 2026), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2). Its large federal awards (ISED research contracts and the CA$23M Canadian Quantum Champions Program award) are civil innovation funding; no National Defence contract was found in the TBS data. This is a weaker inclusion than companies with defence contract evidence; reassess after a documented defence or security customer.

Halifax, NS maker of military and rescue training simulators, courseware and technical publications, with defence forces as its first-listed customer sector. The company's own timeline records hoist mission training systems delivered to RCAF wings at Shearwater (2018) and Comox (2019), a vehicle crew gunnery simulator under the Build in Canada Innovation Program (CA$1M, 2019), a 25-year subcontract to SkyAlyne for the RCAF Future Aircrew Training program (2024), an integrated logistics support subcontract to Seaspan for the Joint Support Ships (2021) and a Lockheed Martin supplier recognition (2021). Government data: a 2026 ACOA Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution of CA$783,750 (a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship) and three 2025-2026 National Defence contract rows matched by name and postal area A1C (CA$32,380; CA$25,875; CA$59,800), with generic descriptions. Training simulators and courseware, not weapons; the gunnery trainer simulates weapon use for training. A stronger inclusion than most: defence is the lead market and several defence customers are named by the company itself.

description.value: Toronto-area launch startup developing a light-lift rocket (R-1) and a reusable medium-lift rocket (R-2) to give Canada sovereign access to orbit, with methane-fuelled engines.

eligibility.rationale: Toronto launch company developing sovereign light- and medium-lift rockets. National Defence announced on 2026-03-16 that Canada Rocket Company is one of three first-round winners of the IDEaS Launch the North contest, conditionally approved for CA$8.3M (project: Canadian Sovereign Launch Capability Development, R1). The contest is run by National Defence's IDEaS programme to build sovereign launch capability for Canada's defence and security needs. BDC's seed investment was tied by BDC Capital to its Defence Platform. A launch company, not a weapons maker. The award is conditional, not a payment, and no contract or grant row exists in the October 2026 government files.

description.value: Ottawa company, founded in 2017, that develops products adding security, connectivity and maintainability to critical real-time networks.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian-owned Ottawa company that designs secure networking and computing equipment 'primarily used in aerospace and defence systems' (its own about page); its Defence applications include intrusion detection, certificate management and RF signal detection. Documented defence relationship: a National Defence contract for application software, CA$697,210 awarded 2026-03-16 (matched by name and postal area K1Z, the same area as the NRC rows that carry its BN); an earlier National Defence contract (CA$227,744.07, 2021, engineering consultants) matches by name only. Secure networking products, not weapons.

description.value: Kitchener maker of autonomous mobile robots: uncrewed ground vehicles for research and field use, and industrial robots through its OTTO Motors division; owned by Rockwell Automation since 2023.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian-HQ (Kitchener, ON, per the company's contact page), foreign-owned since 2023-10-02 (Rockwell Automation, per the acquirer's release; labelled under P-13). Documented defence relationship: a National Defence contract (TBS disclosure; description 'Road motor vehicles'; original CA$312,728.85 from 2022-06-21, CA$622,307.70 after one amendment, reported 2022-23 and 2023-24); matched by name and postal area N2R, and the source row's country field says US, an inconsistency in the source. The acquirer's release lists military among the markets Clearpath serves, and the product line is uncrewed ground and mobile robot platforms for research and industry, not weapons. Earlier National Defence rows (2012-2018) match by name only and are not relied on.

description.value: Ottawa defence technology company building Arctic surveillance and command software (AuraNet) with ruggedised sensors, plus an autonomous collaborative aircraft designed to fly alongside crewed fighters.

eligibility.rationale: Ottawa developer of the AuraNet Arctic surveillance and command software and ruggedised sensors. The company reports that it equipped Canadian Rangers patrols with AuraNet during Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT (eight weeks from February 2026), a self-funded deployment, and the Series A release describes it as deployed with the Canadian Armed Forces. Government data: a CA$0.5M National Research Council IRAP contribution (January to July 2026) for a Phase 0 study of an autonomous collaborative platform and a simulation environment, matched by business number 755463767. No National Defence contract or contract number was found. The company's own claims about the Rangers use are not independently confirmed here.

Vancouver-headquartered earth-observation and analytics company operating a satellite constellation for daily broad-area change detection, with agriculture, forestry, insurance and mining products and a dedicated defence and intelligence offer (persistent change monitoring, tip and cue, maritime domain awareness) and a US federal arm. Government data: a 2024 IDEaS contribution of CA$1,998,550 for an AI wildfire intelligence system supporting first responders (a National Defence challenge on decision support for first responders), and a 2022 National Defence engineering contract of CA$230,000, both matched by name and postal code V6C 0C3, which is also the headquarters address on the company's contact page. Earth observation and analytics, not weapons. Defence is one market of several; the documented Canadian defence relationships are a modest contract and a civil-protection research contribution.

Toronto geospatial-AI company that converts aerial and satellite imagery into vector maps (buildings, roads, land cover), spun out of the University of Waterloo (its own history page). Its own pages list federal, state and municipal government, insurance and telecoms as customers and do not mention defence. The defence case rests on government records: an IDEaS Innovation Networks contribution of CA$4,000,000 titled Ecopia AI GEOINT (2024 to 2026) whose purpose is to help defence and security personnel detect, recognize and identify persons or objects of interest; two National Defence contracts matched by name and postal area M5G (CA$5,806,925, disclosed late, and CA$1,000,000, 2026); and a 2026 CanadaBuys advance contract award notice from the Canadian Armed Forces Mapping and Charting Establishment for a single geospatial AI software solution titled Ecopia Imagery Software (an intent to award; the notice body does not name the vendor). Dual-use mapping software, not weapons. A weaker inclusion on first-party evidence and a stronger one on government evidence: the defence customer is documented by the government, not by the company.

description.value: Halifax developer of satellite platforms and onboard computing for real-time Earth observation, serving commercial, civil and defence customers.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian company (Halifax) building satellites and onboard compute for commercial, civil and defence customers. Documented defence relationship: a CA$2.5M contract from Defence Research and Development Canada under the National Defence IDEaS program to design, build and operate the Canadian Tactical Operations Satellite (CTOS), reported by SpaceQ from the company's statements (September 2025); the TBS data also shows three National Defence contracts to the company, all described as engineering consultants and matched by name and postal area B3J (CA$210,507.50 awarded 2022-10-31; CA$2,874,933.07 awarded 2025-08-27; CA$5,745,872.63 awarded 2026-04-06), and a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution (a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship, A2). The TBS descriptions do not say which project each contract covers, so none is tied to the CTOS contract. Dual-use: orbital compute and satellite platforms; not weapons.

Research candidate per owner decision P-32 (Q10). Documented defence relationship is HISTORICAL: three National Defence disclosure rows to 'GHGSat Incorporated' coded 'Military (R&D)', 2015-2016 (CA$86,148; CA$137,959; CA$114,955). The two 2016 rows share procurement ID W7701-155982/001/QCL and both mention amendments, so they are probably one contract reported twice: at most two distinct contracts, and the three values must not be added. No further National Defence rows were found under the GHGSat name after 2016. GHGSat is a commercial emissions-monitoring company, not primarily defence-focused. ENTITY CHECK (P-32): Corporations Canada lists one federal corporation, GHGSat Incorporated (number 805744-3, BN 840066500), incorporated 2011-12-19 and never renamed, so the vendor name on the 2015-2016 rows is that corporation's exact legal name. The old rows themselves carry no postal code or BN, so the link rests on the exact legal name; a same-named provincial entity was not ruled out.

description.value: Maritime intelligence company, now branded OCIANA, whose platform fuses vessel, sensor and environmental data to predict maritime activity for defence and security agencies and port supply chains.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian maritime-intelligence software and data company (formerly GSTS, now OCIANA). Documented defence relationship: repeated National Defence contracts in the TBS data, 2021-2025, described as engineering and IT consulting (for example CA$3,504,986.20 awarded 2025-08-26 and CA$555,151.83 awarded 2023-06-02), matched by name and the Dartmouth postal area B2Y; plus a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from ACOA (a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship, A2). The company positions the platform for naval defence, border security and coast guard use; its 31 August 2026 release says OCIANA delivers dual-use capabilities, including a predictive maritime intelligence layer for defence and security organizations; and the ACOA release says the system serves military, civil and commercial sectors. Data and analytics products, not weapons.

Mississauga, ON maker of electrodeposited nanocrystalline metal ('Nanovate') products; its home page lists Aerospace and Defense among its markets. Documented defence relationship: National Defence contracts coded 'Military (R&D)' in 2011, 2012 and 2014 (CA$44,722; CA$565,000; CA$564,887; matched by name only, with no postal code or BN), Strategic Aerospace and Defence Initiative contributions from ISED (2007-2013, carrying the BN), and two IDEaS awards (CA$200,000 in 2020, and CA$833,750 in 2022 for an easy-clean antiviral coating under National Defence's 'Super sanitize' challenge). Materials and coatings, not weapons.

description.value: Toronto company that designs, builds and operates a satellite constellation relaying data between spacecraft in orbit, with optical links and in-house satellite production.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian-HQ satellite data-relay operator (Toronto, first-party). Documented defence relationships: a National Defence engineering contract (TBS disclosure, 2026), a FedDev Ontario Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution (2025; a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship, A2), and, per the company, an air-to-space optical demonstration with the Space Development Agency and General Atomics (September 2025). Commercial connectivity is the core business: dual-use, non-weapon. Owner Q1 (P-22): research candidate.

description.value: Boisbriand company that designs and manufactures robotic arms for assistive, medical, research and industrial uses, including manipulators for uncrewed ground platforms used in EOD and CBRN work.

eligibility.rationale: Boisbriand, QC maker of robotic arms (rooted in assistive and research robotics, now also industrial and professional uses). Documented defence and security product line: the company's own defence page presents its arms as manipulators for uncrewed ground platforms in explosive-ordnance disposal, CBRN response, demining and remote inspection for the Canadian Armed Forces and allied forces, and says they are fielded with Remotec ANDROS EOD robots and by Turkish Gendarmerie teams through integrators (company statements). Also a CED Regional Defence Investment Initiative (SME) contribution of CA$2,500,000 (2026; defence-program funding, not a customer relationship, A2). No National Defence contract was found under this name. Protective and disposal tasks, no weapons payload (P-15: company-level facts only).

description.value: Fredericton developer of mixed-reality remote-support software that connects frontline workers with remote experts for equipment maintenance and repair, including defence sustainment.

eligibility.rationale: Fredericton, NB company (founded 2016 per its about page) selling remote-expert, connected-worker software and support; its Defence page describes equipment sustainment and fielding support for military, OEM and industry partners. Documented defence relationship: repeated National Defence contracts in the TBS data, for example computer-systems-security R&D (CA$827,438.80, 2019, matched by name only), software licence and maintenance fees (CA$1,153,785.00, 2020, name only) and later licence rows in 2025 matched by name and postal area E3C (CA$14,690.00 and CA$13,000.00). Software and support services, not weapons. The 2019-2020 DND rows lack a postal code or BN, so they rest on the exact name.

description.value: Canadian operating subsidiary of Kraken Robotics, formerly Kraken Sonar Systems, created in 2012 to commercialize synthetic aperture sonar; based in Mount Pearl, Newfoundland and Labrador.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian operating subsidiary of the listed Kraken Robotics Inc. (wholly owned per the parent's FY2025 statements). Documented defence relationship: two National Defence contracts in the TBS data, 'Ships and boats' (CA$33,689,621.80 net after amendments) and 'Ships and boats Parts' (CA$12,259,675), both with start date 2022-11-30, matched by legal name and postal area A1N; the TBS descriptions are generic categories and say nothing about the equipment. Its NRC-funded projects are sonar and uncrewed-underwater-vehicle development. Sensors and uncrewed systems, not weapons.

description.value: Listed parent of the Kraken group, which supplies sonar and optical sensors, subsea batteries, and underwater robotics equipment and services for military and commercial applications.

eligibility.rationale: Canadian-HQ, publicly listed (TSXV: PNG) subsea sensor, battery and underwater-robotics company. Its audited statements describe the principal business as supplying sonar and optical sensors, batteries and underwater robotics equipment and services for military and commercial applications, and its wholly owned subsidiary Kraken Robotic Systems Inc. holds National Defence contracts in the TBS data (see that organization). Products are sensors, power and uncrewed systems, not weapons. After the subsequent-event acquisition of Covelya Group (closed 2026-07-02 per the company) the group is much larger; this record covers Kraken Robotics Inc. as reported through FY2025 and Q2 2026.

financing.latestStage: Bought deal public offering of subscription receipts

eligibility.rationale: Laval, QC repair, maintenance, manufacturing and engineering provider for civil and military aircraft (composite and sheet-metal structures, radomes, nacelles, flight control surfaces). Its own pages say it serves the RCAF, the USAF and other defence organizations, offers readiness, sustainment and modernization support, and record Canadian Controlled Goods Program approval in 2013 to work on military programs and US/Canada Joint Certification Program approval in 2015 for US military contracts. Government data: a 2026 CED Regional Defence Investment Initiative (SME) contribution of CA$5,000,000, matched by business number and postal code; this is a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship. No National Defence contract row was matched by business number or postal code. Aircraft maintenance and manufacturing, not weapons. A weaker inclusion on the documented evidence: defence is one of two markets (civil aviation is the other) and no named defence customer contract was found.

Markham, ON developer of orbital launch vehicles (Tundra, Tempest), a suborbital pathfinder (Taiga), 3D-printed liquid rocket engines, a spaceport in Newfoundland and Labrador and small satellites, founded in 2022 and describing itself as privately funded and fully Canadian owned. Defence relationship, documented by the company and by the government: in March 2026 the Department of National Defence selected it as a winner of the IDEaS Launch the North challenge with a Phase 1 award of CA$8,333,333 (grant record matched by business number 721893303 and postal code), a National Defence engineering contract of CA$287,432.38 (2026, matched by name and postal area L3R), and a named partnership list that includes the Canadian Association of Defence and Security Industries. WEAPONS-ADJACENT PROGRAM FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER: its SHARP program (Arrow rocket-powered UAV, described as capable of research, reconnaissance or intercept missions; Sabre hypersonic sub-orbital rocket; M2S-HyRock hypersonic engine) is marketed for defence research and commercial testing. Launch is the primary business and SHARP is described as derived from the launch systems, so this record does not treat the company as a weapons maker; the owner should confirm.

description.value: Montreal maker of photon-counting low-light cameras, based on technology first developed for space astronomy, used in space, astronomy, biomedical imaging, night vision and quantum applications.

eligibility.rationale: Montréal maker of ultra-sensitive low-light cameras for ground and space use; its own site lists 'Space & Defense' as an application area. Documented defence relationship: a National Defence contract described as engineering consultants, CA$2,475,772.90 awarded 2026-03-02, matched by name and postal area H3C (the same area as the grant rows carrying its BN); an earlier National Defence contract (CA$142,665.58, 2020, imaging equipment) matches by name only. Also a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from CED (2026), a defence-program contribution rather than a customer relationship (A2). Imaging sensors, not weapons.

Montréal designer of programmable chips and wireless and RF equipment; its home page is titled 'Advanced Wireless and RF Solutions for Defense & Law Enforcement' and its menu has a Defence section. Documented defence-program link: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative (SME) contribution from CED (CA$4,500,000, 2026), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2). No National Defence contract was found under this name in the TBS data. Wireless and RF products, not weapons. Whether it has any foreign owner is not established.

Longueuil, QC developer of the Aurora small-satellite launch vehicle (patented hybrid propulsion, now storable liquid propellants), founded 2017. Its own defence page presents a sovereign, ITAR-free, containerized responsive launch capability for intelligence, surveillance, Arctic awareness, satellite communications and navigation missions, and its 2025 release says the technology serves commercial and defence satellite markets and national security applications including hypersonic platforms. Government data: a 2026 IDEaS Launch the North Phase 1 award of CA$8,333,333 for the Aurora-8 responsive launch vehicle, matched by business number 844028092. A launch company, not a weapons maker; the mention of hypersonic platforms as a supported application is noted for the owner. A sovereign-launch company with defence as a stated market and a National Defence award.

St. John's, NL maker of marine radar systems for oil, ice and small-target detection and wave monitoring; a 2024 company release says it is collaborating on equipment for a new Canadian Coast Guard icebreaker. Documented defence relationship is thin: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from ACOA (CA$1,000,000, 2026), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2), and three National Defence contracts (2010 architectural and engineering services, 2016 science-and-technology R&D CA$106,967, 2019 engineering consultants CA$25,000) that match by name only. Environmental monitoring qualifies only with documented security or defence use (P-12), and that evidence is limited; treat as a weak inclusion and reassess after a first-party description of defence or security customers.

Collingwood, ON and Dartmouth, NS maker of piezoceramic materials, hydrophones and acoustic sensors for underwater use. Its own defence page lists its components as integrated in hull-mounted sonar, mine countermeasures, sonobuoys, towed arrays, anti-torpedo countermeasures and dipping sonar, and says it serves navies and military forces; its history says its in-house formulations were perfected to meet Navy standards. Civil markets (energy, aquaculture, oceanography, hydrography) are listed too. Government data: a 2025 ACOA Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution of CA$1,950,000, matched by business number and postal code (a defence-program contribution, not a customer relationship). No National Defence contract row was matched by business number or postal code. A supplier of sensing components; it does not make weapons. One item is weapons-adjacent and is flagged for the owner: components for an anti-torpedo countermeasure. Defence is its first-listed industry, so the inclusion rests mainly on the company's own statements.

Mount Pearl, NL maker of wireless power transfer systems; its Aerospace & Defense page describes military-grade wireless power systems, ITAR-free, and its news list says it joined the NORTHERN UxV Consortium to advance Canadian defence autonomy (June 2026). Documented defence-program link: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from ACOA (CA$4,000,000, 2026), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2). Boeing invested CA$10.3 million in the company (release dated 2025-01-23) as part of its Industrial and Technological Benefits commitment for Canada's P-8A Poseidon purchase, and the company's news list reports a seventh Boeing contract of US$3.8 million (December 2025). No National Defence contract appears in the TBS data under this name. Power electronics, not weapons.

Montréal maker of satellite ground and broadband networking equipment. Its Defense & Government page says it has designed ground networking technology for government and defence customers for over three decades and lists defence uses such as beyond-line-of-sight battlefield communications, naval communications and UAV communications. Documented defence-program link: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative (SME) contribution from CED (CA$1,250,000, 2026), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2). No National Defence contract was found in the TBS data. Communications equipment, not weapons. Ownership (federal register, read 2026-10-14): two individuals with significant control, who hold the shares directly and indirectly (one more than 50 percent up to 75 percent, the other at least 25 percent up to 50 percent, both since 2017-12-04); no corporate shareholder or foreign parent is listed. The company lists R&D and support centres in several countries.

Mississauga, ON research and software company in multisensor, multitarget tracking and sensor-data fusion (video, EO/IR, radar, sonar, AIS/ADS-B), selling licensed software and consulting; its own pages describe ground, maritime, transportation, search-and-rescue and crowd-monitoring uses and name no defence customer. The defence relationship is documented by government records, matched by exact name and postal area L5M: a 2025 IDEaS contribution of CA$1,000,000 for a symbolic-AI swarm interface for surveillance with human command and control (the NORAD Modernization contest), and National Defence engineering-consultant contracts of CA$1,149,954 (2022) and CA$1,149,965.50 (2024), plus two smaller ones of about CA$230,000 and a CA$1,149,931 row under the spelling TrackGen Solution Inc. Tracking and sensor-processing software, not weapons. The inclusion rests on government evidence; the company's own pages are generic.

description.value: Paradise, Newfoundland and Labrador maker of marine safety training simulators, offering simulation-based training to offshore energy, defence and security, ferry and shipping customers and schools.

eligibility.rationale: Privately held Paradise, NL maker of maritime safety and navigation training simulators (lifeboat, fast rescue boat, ice management). Its home page says it helps regulatory bodies and defence partners worldwide and lists defence and security among the industries it serves. Documented defence relationship: six National Defence contracts in the TBS data in 2025-2026, matched by name and postal area A1L, with generic descriptions (computer equipment CA$449,123.52; other equipment CA$255,760.00; image and video communications equipment CA$222,764.20; training packages and tuition rows of CA$15,497.84, CA$24,852.00 and CA$37,089.27). The descriptions do not say what was supplied. Also contracts with Fisheries and Oceans, NRC and Public Works. Training simulators, not weapons. A weaker inclusion: defence is one of several markets.

Aurora, Ontario maker of rugged high-performance embedded computing (VPX and related boards) that describes its market as aerospace, defense and other rugged deployments, holds AS9100D and ITAR 126.5 compliance and lists CMMC Level 2 readiness (its own about page). Documented defence-program link: a Regional Defence Investment Initiative contribution from FedDev Ontario (2025-26), which shows participation in a defence program, not a customer relationship (A2). No National Defence contract appears under this BN or name in the TBS data. Ownership (federal register, read 2026-10-14): a single individual with significant control, who is also a director, holds more than 75 percent of the shares directly (since 1999); no corporate shareholder or foreign parent is listed. The company says it manufactures in Canada and the United States; no US entity was identified. Embedded computing hardware, not weapons.
